posts.name: flamethrower49
posts.cooked:
Ameena:

Not necessarily - Mr Fixer with Driving Mantis and a Pipe Wrench can redirect Iron Legacy's end-of-turn damage back to himself, as long as Iron Legacy isn't buffed. That combo plus Harmony makes Strike deal three damage, so if you play Overdrive that's six damage in a turn. Alternatively you could play Charge and deal four with that, plus three from Strike for a total of seven damage (as long as Leggy doesn't have any soak, of course).

Fixer can probably do better than a plan that relies on Legacy not having any buffs OR soak.  I'd forgo the Driving Mantis in this fight.

Random teams certainly aren't taboo against Iron Legacy.  I have a decent win record against the advanced version of him playing random teams.  There is probably a way for any group of heroes to win, even though it might take very specific draws, or incapacitated shenanigans, or no small amount of beating your head against brick walls.  It's certainly not your average recreational activity.

The teams that would do worst are the teams with zero ongoing destruction or the teams with miniscule damage.  It also seems like he doesn't scale quite as well as some villains - that is, a 3-hero team will have a much tougher time than a 5-hero team.  This is especially if the normal strategy against him is debuff him for a couple rounds, then one-turn him from >20 to zero on turn 3 or 4, right before he kills you.  Three characters just won't be as efficient at that.

So… who is good at him?  Anyone with a good amount of damage and a few ways to remove ongoings are probably the best.

I think the members of the Freedom Six are generally good at him, except Unity, who'll just have an infernally tough time keeping bots out.   I would avoid Omnitron-X (I'm talking advanced here - Plating is worthless and he can't keep components, unless you choose to flip him).  I'd avoid the Scholar in this fight against irreducible damage, since he also lacks ongoing removal and doesn't typically bring a large amount of damage.  Chrono-Ranger and Expatriette have good options.  Nightmist is always good, but she has to be on the ball to not die right away.  Fanatic has some good options in the fight as well.  Argent Adept and Visionary can field the ongoing destruction, but not so much the damage.  Ra, Haka, and Legacy can field plenty of damage, but not the ongoing destruction.   I would probably avoid Fixer - his damage isn't especially high very quickly, and he lacks ongoing destruction.

That was too long.

Spiff:

Yeah, the Operative has Fixer's icon, just like the Chairman.  That means that if the Operative were ever to punch the Chairman, their shared hatred of Fixer would cause Operative's punch to hurt more.

It is not just a "nemesis" icon, it is a hero icon. In the case of Chairman and Operative, the Operative would not strike the Chairman for an extra point of damage because the Chairman is not Mr. Fixer.  With the Ennead, same applies, they would not hit eachother for more damage. 

The ONLY way you might be able to argue otherwise would be a thematic argument allowing Anubis (Ra's icon) to deal extra damage to the rest of the Ennead. But, also Consider the case of Plauge Rat and the Final Wasteland enviroment, where that same thematic argument for the above would lead to a different mechanical conclusion, as the pack rats may not attack one of their own (much less the "alpha" rat, so to speak).

Given all of that, I think it is safe to say that the nemesis mechanic is stricktly a relationship between any given hero target and a non-hero target that shares its Hero icon
